findings.statement: The currently retrieved arXiv v1 abstract attributes introduction of the term mesa-optimization to the paper’s authors.
findings.qualification: This authenticates the currently served version’s wording, not independent historical priority. v3 repeats the substantive assertion.

findings.statement: The 2022 date displayed by the currently served v1 PDF is consistent with later typesetting rather than a 2022 initial submission.
premises: Current PDF title and creation metadata agreement
findings.qualification: Compilation-dependent source date and creation metadata explain the discrepancy plausibly. No compilation log or original 2019 PDF proves the precise regeneration history. Submission, title and file dates remain separate.

findings.statement: The upstream catalog’s alleged arXiv v4 supports the recorded abstract wording.
findings.qualification: No v4 expression was obtained. Both paths fail and current history ends at v3. Treat v4 as an unsubstantiated catalog identity; do not fabricate a comparison or infer historical nonexistence.

findings.statement: The originally cited post ID aW288uWABwTruBmgF identifies Soares’s Sharp Left Turn post.
findings.qualification: The retained original proposition is contradicted by the retrieved wrong object. The conflicting catalog ID 7W8HqksjBXDcKkrD7 remains unidentified, not an alias proved by its slug.

findings.statement: GNhMPAWcfBCASy8e6 is the intended identifiable Sharp Left Turn expression by Nate Soares.
findings.qualification: Title, opening self-attribution and relevant argument match the intended citation. Displayed publication is 15 June 2022. Original publication-day bytes and first use of the phrase remain unestablished.

findings.statement: The current CEV institutional reprint attributes the work to 2004 and contains the exact full name.
findings.qualification: Earliest bibliographically dated exact-name candidate found in this selected corpus: the work attributed to 2004, observed only in a later reprint. This is not an authenticated 2004 exact-name occurrence or an unrestricted first use.

findings.statement: The exact term Coherent Extrapolated Volition had its first historical use in 2004.
findings.qualification: No authenticated contemporary exact-name occurrence was found in the bounded 2001–2004 corpus. Zero matches in 355 subject-selected SL4 bodies is a screen result, not archive-wide absence. Reprint attribution cannot settle literal period wording or priority.

findings.statement: Creating Friendly AI 1.0 is an earlier conceptual candidate involving volition-based Friendliness.
premises: Explicit treatment of volition and goal content
Exact full-name screen negative in current extracted text
findings.qualification: Bibliographically dated 15 June 2001, inspected in a later reprint. Conceptual antecedence is a research classification, not exact-term use or proof of transmission.

findings.statement: Surviving period-labelled announcements identify the 2004 essay as Collective Volition.
findings.qualification: SL4 announcement is dated 31 May; Foresight is dated 11 June. Both are current renderings, not independently authenticated 2004 captures. A reply’s contradictory date prevents ranking all message headers as reliable chronology.

findings.statement: A documented transmission chain connects the 2001 conceptual treatment to the exact later CEV name.
findings.qualification: Shared authorship and conceptual similarity do not establish that chain. SL4 replies and Foresight’s quotation document particular carriers of the Collective Volition announcement only; they do not date a renaming or establish broad influence.

findings.statement: SL4 reply 8894 displays an apparent calendar-date discrepancy.
findings.qualification: The archive header displays 30 May; the quoted original displays 31 May without a timezone. These cannot be normalized confidently. A timezone difference could explain the apparent ordering; no chronological impossibility, error cause or corrected date is established. Do not rank priority using either header alone.

corrections.rationale: Split v1 from the unsubstantiated v4 catalog label and separately observed v3. Preserve old catalog value in a correction history; retain stable source/work IDs only with expression-level migration rules.
Replace the overloaded date field with explicitly typed dates; original submission date is not erroneous. Do not date the underlying work to 2022.
Keep this source as the wrong-object evidence. Quarantine 7W as unidentified. Create a separate GNh expression for the intended work; never relabel the wrong-object record as Soares.
The baseline 2022 date conflicts with the matched wrong-object post metadata. Preserve it as superseded reporting; this correction is not a publication-day archive authentication.

search.question: What exact-name occurrences and earlier conceptual candidates can this bounded author/venue corpus establish?

search.selection: All 48 monthly date indexes; retrieve numeric message links with subjects matching /volition|summary of current FAI/i. This is a title-screened subset, not full-text search of the entire archive.
search.normalization: Strip HTML tags in Hypermail body markers (fallback whole page), collapse whitespace, case-insensitive /coherent\s+extrapolated\s+volition/; manually inspect positive/candidate contexts. HTML entities and PDF extraction may hide variants.
